content:
Florence Pugh warned that she’s “not standing for bullshit behavior” on film sets anymore.

In a new interview with Elle magazine, Pugh got candid about the lessons she’s learned since her professional film debut at age 17 in 2014’s “The Falling.” The British actress told the publication that she’s gotten “better and better” at protecting herself in Hollywood.

“Every time I work on a movie, I get more confident in the way that I can protect myself and the way that I can lead a film set, and just not stand for bullshit anymore. I’m not doing it,” she said in the Nov. 10 interview.

“I’m not standing for bullshit behavior. I’m not standing for bullshit attitude[s]. I’m not allowing for people to be rude to the crew,” Pugh continued.

Pugh explained that “you just get bolder and bigger and more confident with time” in her industry and it makes “you want to be around and work with the right people.”

“And the moment someone is making that vibe feel off, everybody feels it. I don’t want to deal with messy,” she declared.

The Oscar nominee put it simply, telling the outlet, “It’s just about surrounding yourself with professionals who have the same way of working in mind: Show up on time, don’t be rude, don’t be a misogynist.”

Earlier in the interview, Pugh confronted Hollywood’s unfair beauty standards and stereotypes against women.

“There’s so much scrutiny of how we look, how we dress, and how we age. And then when we do those things, they’re like, ‘Oh my God, she looks like this, or she’s done too much of that, or she’s gained weight, or she’s lost too much weight.’ You can never get any footing right.”

The Marvel star argued that she’s done her best work on screen when she “truly feel[s] ugly.”

Pugh added, “When I’ve got shit makeup on and I’m either sick or ugly or having a hangover or a breakdown. I love that type of makeup because it allows me to be free.”
